subject: math

objective.text: Use math drawings to compose a rectangle with square tiles.

explanations.title: Trace a unit square
explanations.text: Trace one tile to draw a square. Trace it again beside the first one to make a row. Then start the next row below.

explanations.title: Shared lines
explanations.text: You do not trace the whole square again. The bottom line of the first square is the top line of the next square.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1 (S: The bottom line from the first square...)

explanations.title: Like making a ruler
explanations.text: Drawing an array is like making a ruler. We repeat a unit and make the spaces the same. This time the unit is a square.

explanations.title: Draw without a tile
explanations.text: Draw each line about as long as the side of the first square. Draw the top, the bottom and then close the square. All the squares should look the same.

explanations.title: Rectangle or square
explanations.text: 2 rows of 3 makes a rectangle. 3 rows of 3 makes a square.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 2 (S: A square! ... A rectangle!)

explanations.title: Compensation
explanations.text: Make one number a ten. Take 1 from 42 and give it to 19. Then 42 plus 19 becomes 41 plus 20, which is 61.

examples.title: 2 rows of 3 by tracing
examples.text: Trace a tile 3 times for a row. Trace 3 more below it for the second row. 3 plus 3 equals 6.

examples.title: 3 rows of 3 by drawing
examples.text: Draw one square. Draw lines the same length to make 3 squares in a row. Make 3 rows. It is a square.

examples.title: 42 plus 19
examples.text: 19 needs 1 more to make 20. Take 1 from 42. 41 plus 20 equals 61.
